No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Gombe 2027: Seven Pillar Manifesto: What APC’s Jamilu Gwamna Promises Voters by Babaji Usman Babaji 12 seconds ago in North East , News , Politics Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Gombe State , Dr Jamil Isyaku Gwamna, has on Monday unveiled his development manifesto ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The seven-pillar manifesto, titled IMPACTS: A Greater Gombe Together, outlines his development agenda around seven critical sectors, with a headline commitment to create 100,000 net new jobs within four years if elected.
Gwamna describes the document as a covenant with the people, promising to manage public funds prudently, sustain ongoing development projects and govern with fairness, irrespective of political, religious or ethnic differences.
The seven pillars, represented by the acronym IMPACTS, are Infrastructure and Essential Services; Manufacturing and Industrialisation; People and Human Capital; Agriculture and Rural Transformation; Commerce and Trade; Technology and Digital Inclusion; and Security and Environment.
Under the first pillar, Infrastructure and Essential Services, Gwamna promises to complete ongoing projects, expand road networks, improve water supply and sanitation, and strengthen public infrastructure maintenance.
His proposals include constructing an additional 1,000 kilometres of roads, completing the Gombe Regional Water Project, constructing or refurbishing 50 boreholes in each LCDA and developing a 100-megawatt solar power plant through private-sector investment.
The second pillar, Manufacturing and Industrialisation, seeks to move Gombe from exporting raw agricultural products to processing and exporting finished goods.
He proposes operationalising the Special Agro-Livestock Development Zone, completing Phase Two of the Muhammadu Buhari Industrial Park and establishing at least three industrial or agro-processing clusters, promising to create 10,000 direct manufacturing jobs and 50,000 indirect jobs through industrialisation and agricultural value chains.
Under the third pillar, People and Human Capital Development, Gwamna focuses on education, healthcare, youth empowerment, women, children, sports and civil service reforms.
He promises to return 400,000 out-of-school children to classrooms, recruit 1,000 teachers, train 10,000 existing teachers, upgrade at least 60 per cent of public basic schools and provide scholarships to 10,000 students from poor households.
In healthcare, he plans to maintain at least two fully functioning primary healthcare facilities in every ward, establish three general hospitals across the state’s senatorial districts, recruit 500 health workers and expand Go-Health coverage to one million beneficiaries.
He also proposes a Youth Enterprise Fund, vocational training, 35 per cent representation for women in government appointments and 40 per cent inclusion of young people in governance.
The fourth pillar, Agriculture and Rural Transformation, targets increased agricultural production, irrigation, mechanisation, livestock development and improved rural livelihoods.
The proposals include expanding irrigation around Dadin Kowa, Balanga and Cham dams, establishing 110 agricultural clusters, deploying 300 extension officers and reducing post-harvest losses by 25 per cent.
He also plans to establish a Ministry of Livestock Development, modernise grazing reserves and support 100 functional dairy cooperatives, with a target of creating 20,000 jobs across the livestock value chain.
For the fifth pillar, Commerce and Trade, Gwamna wants to strengthen small businesses, modernise markets and position Gombe as Northern Nigeria’s leading commercial centre after Kano.
He promises to support at least 50,000 small and medium-scale enterprises, rehabilitate major markets, establish a one-stop business registration desk and promote tourism through investments in Dadin Kowa Dam, Tula Highlands, Tangale Hills and other attractions.
The sixth pillar, Technology and Digital Inclusion, focuses on expanding broadband connectivity, improving digital literacy and using technology to make government services more accessible.
Through a proposed Gombe Digital Opportunities and Advancement programme, he promises to train at least 150,000 young people in digital skills and support 100,000 verified digital income opportunities.
The manifesto also proposes a public e-governance portal through which residents can access government services, submit complaints and monitor public projects, budgets and procurement activities.
The seventh pillar, Security and Environment, combines community security interventions with environmental protection and climate adaptation.
Gwamna proposes training 1,000 community-based environmental rangers, planting four million trees within four years, establishing farmer-herder peace councils in every LCDA and strengthening community policing arrangements.
He also promises to rehabilitate at least 10 high-risk gully sites and 20 priority drainage corridors to reduce flooding and erosion.
Beyond the seven development pillars, the candidate identifies four governing principles that he says will guide his administration: accountability, continuity, fiscal discipline and inclusion.
On accountability, he promises to publish an annual public scorecard showing what his government promised, what it delivered and what remains outstanding.
He also proposes a project-status dashboard displaying project locations, budgets, contractors, completion percentages and photographs, alongside budget performance reports, audited financial statements and citizen feedback reports.
On continuity, Gwamna pledges to protect, complete and expand Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s projects and programmes, saying he will not abandon existing initiatives that are working.
He also promises fiscal discipline, describing the Yahaya administration’s financial management as a foundation he intends to maintain, while ensuring that public spending produces lasting benefits.
On inclusion, he pledges that no individual or community will be left behind because of geography, gender, ethnicity, religion or social status.
In his personal pledge, Gwamna promises to manage public funds with accountability and prudence, listen to both supporters and critics, and govern with justice and fairness.
“I will work very hard to leave Gombe better than I found it,” he declares.
The manifesto also commits him to translating the proposals into annual delivery plans, assigning responsibilities to ministries, departments and agencies, with approved budgets, measurable milestones and public reporting timelines.
However, for political commentators like Mohammed Aliyu, despite its detailed promises, Gwamna’s IMPACTS manifesto leaves major questions about funding, feasibility and implementation. It proposes costly projects, including 1,000 kilometres of roads, 10,000 affordable homes, a 100MW solar plant and three industrial clusters, but does not provide a consolidated estimate of their costs or explain how the state would finance them.
He added that several commitments also depend on private investors, federal agencies and development partners, without clear details of what would happen if the expected support does not materialise.
Aliyu argued that the document does not provide enough detail on how competing priorities would be funded and coordinated, particularly where programmes require sustained recurrent spending, stressing that its credibility will depend on realistic implementation plans and independent monitoring of results.
